name: cua
description: Scale computer-use 2.0 with open-source drivers, cross-OS fleets, and benchmarks for training, evaluation, and data generation.
one_liner: Gives an AI agent its own virtual computer it can click around, type into, and take screenshots of, so it can operate normal desktop apps the way a human would.
buyer: An automation agency owner who currently pays staff to click through legacy desktop or web apps that have no API, and wants to replace that manual work with an agent.
business_use_cases: An outsourcing shop automates repetitive back-office data entry into an old Windows desktop app that was never given an API.
A QA team spins up isolated cloud desktops to run automated UI regression tests across macOS, Windows, and Linux builds.
A researcher builds and sells a benchmark or training-data pack for evaluating computer-use agents on a specific vertical (e.g. insurance claims software).

money_ideas.idea: Offer 'RPA replacement' automation services for businesses stuck on GUI-only legacy software.
Sell managed cloud-desktop capacity plus pre-built automation recipes to teams evaluating computer-use agents.

steal_this: Pick one tedious GUI-only workflow (e.g. exporting reports from an old accounting app) and ship a paid weekend automation for a single small-business client.
